newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Albright warns Iraq it could lose oil sales deal.
newsitem.headline: Albright warns Iraq it could lose oil sales deal.

text.p: Madeleine Albright, the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, on Wednesday warned that Iraq could lose the oil-for-food deal if President Saddam Hussein did not honor his committments.
"If Saddam Hussein does not live up to his part of the bargain on resolution 986, it won't stay in effect," she said in reference to the 1995 Security Council resolution that set up the plan.
Albright was responding to a heckler during hearings by the Senate Foreign Relations Committee on her nomination to be secretary of state.

Resolution 986 allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months in order to buy food, medicine and other necessities for his people, suffering under the effect of trade sanctions. The embargoes were imposed in August 1990 when Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait.
The resolution went into effect on December 10 and comes up for renewal in six months. It provides for heavy U.N. monitoring to make sure the food is distributed equitably.

"I am as concerned about the children of Iraq as is Saddam Hussein, who used his people as a pawn in order to try to break what is a legitimate sanctions regime that was imposed on his coutnry as a result of his aggression into Kuwait," she said.

"So the issue here is that Saddam Hussein is the one who has the fate of his country in his hand and he is the one who is responsible for the starving children, not the United States in America," she added.
Asked by Senator Jesse Helms if her position on Iraq had been discussed with President Clinton, she said, "Absolutely. This is the policy of the United States."
